findings.title: Device is cached before database limit check, bypassing the limit on subsequent requests
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)`. When the anonymous device limit has been reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request is rejected in `Anonymous.Authenticate`. However, because the device's cache key is already stored in `localCache` (with a 29-minute TTL), any subsequent request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` will hit the cache at line 83, cause `tagDeviceUI` to return `nil`, and allow the anonymous user to authenticate despite exceeding the device limit. `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

findings.title: MySQL `RowsAffected` returns 0 when updated values are unchanged, falsely triggering `ErrDeviceLimitReached`
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, `result.RowsAffected()` is checked for `0` to determine if the device did not exist in the active window and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` should be returned. On MySQL (when `clientFoundRows` is not enabled in the DSN, which is the default), `UPDATE` returns `0` rows affected if a matching row is found but the column values (`client_ip`, `user_agent`, `updated_at`) are identical to the existing values in the database. Since MySQL's `DATETIME` / `TIMESTAMP` columns in Grafana have 1-second precision, if an already-registered device makes two requests within the same second (e.g., before caching or across instances) with the same IP and User-Agent while at the device limit, `RowsAffected()` will be `0` and the valid device will be rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

findings.title: `untagDevice` does not evict the device from `localCache` on login
findings.body: When a user logs in, the post-login hook `untagDevice` deletes their device from `anon_device` in the database so it no longer counts toward the anonymous device limit. However, `untagDevice` does not remove the device key from `a.localCache`. If the user logs out within the 29-minute cache TTL and continues browsing anonymously while the instance is at `deviceLimit`, `tagDeviceUI` will see the cached key and return `nil` without re-inserting the device or checking the limit, allowing an untracked anonymous session.
